first_impression.reaction: My assistant read it first. Her summary: a careful, general cost guide for Australian couples comparing quotes. The opening is calm and doesn't try to sell me a cheap number, which I respect: 'The Greece wedding cost you will be quoted depends on decisions only you can make'. But nothing on the first screen says this team has done a wedding of 300 guests, a closed property or a family that needs privacy. I wouldn't read past the intro myself. She flagged the exclusive use section for me and that's all I looked at.

journey.quote: The Greece wedding cost you will be quoted depends on decisions only you can make: which island, what kind of venue, which month and day, how many guests fly in, and how much of their travel and accommodation you cover.
journey.reaction: Understated, no hard sell, no 'affordable'. That tone works for me. But it reads as written for someone checking a budget, not for someone asking what's possible.

journey.quote: Ask each supplier which currency the quote, deposit and balance are invoiced in, when each payment falls due and what happens to money paid if plans change.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but that's my family office's job, not mine. Four bullet points of admin before anything about the experience itself.

journey.quote: Ask whether exclusive use, where your party is the only one on site, is offered, for how many nights, and whether it needs a minimum number of rooms or guests.
journey.reaction: This is the only part written for me. Good that it's there. But it stops at 'ask'. Nothing about closing the property to the public, security, or keeping photos off social media.

journey.quote: Ask, too, whether another wedding can be held there the same day.
journey.reaction: Fine for a normal couple. For us, the idea of sharing the day with another wedding is off the table, so this is the wrong question to finish on.

journey.quote: Guest numbers touch catering, drinks, transfers and the space you need.
journey.reaction: One line on guests, with no sign that 200 to 400 people is something the writer has thought about. Nothing on staffing, catering for family customs, or managing guests flying in from three countries.

journey.quote: Who books and pays for transfers on the day, and for arrivals and departures?
journey.reaction: Ferries, cancelled ferries, an extra night. My guests won't be on public ferries. No mention of private transfers.

journey.section: What packages include and what sits outside them
journey.quote: Read the contents, not the package name.
journey.reaction: Good advice, but the whole section is package language: what's in the bundle, what's an add-on. This is exactly the standard package client conversation I'm trying to avoid.

journey.section: Paying for a wedding in Greece from Australia
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and has inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: We're in Dubai and London as much as Sydney. 'Australian couples' tells me this is not built around a family like mine.

journey.quote: A change of mind gives no right to a refund under the consumer guarantees, though a business with a change of mind policy must follow it.
journey.reaction: Our lawyers handle contracts. A long consumer law section makes the brand feel like it is writing for first-time buyers worried about losing a deposit.

journey.section: Planning your Greece wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' is good. 'One Wedded Advisor' for 400 guests and a multi-day event worries me. Who's the team behind them? And nothing here proves they've handled my scale.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland delivered weddings of 200 to 400 guests, and can they show that privately?
Can they arrange for a whole property to be closed to the public across several days?
How do they work with a family's own security team and the venue's security?
How do they handle confidentiality: NDAs for suppliers, no-phone policies, keeping guest lists and photos off social media and away from press?
Do they arrange private transfers, yachts or helicopters rather than public ferries?
Can they handle catering and customs for families from different cultures, for example halal catering or multi-day family celebrations?
Is there a private or referral channel to enquire, rather than a general concierge form?
Who is on the team behind the single Wedded Advisor for an event this size?

turn_offs_found.quote: Our guide to [Greece wedding packages and what they include](/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) shows how venues set them out, and [all inclusive Greece wedding packages compared](/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive) covers the broader bundles.
turn_offs_found.why: Package and bundle language. It tells me I'd be treated like a standard package client.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask whether each item is inside the package, an add-on or not offered:
turn_offs_found.why: More package framing. At my level nothing is an add-on; it is either possible or it isn't.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask for every contract in English, with a copy you keep. If the binding version is in Greek, ask which version prevails if the two differ, and have anything unclear read before you sign.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. A long string of 'ask' instructions throughout feels a little eager and aimed at people doing this themselves.

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-cost&utm_content=closing), and for more ideas, read [the Get Wedded magazine](/magazine?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-cost&utm_content=magnet).
cta_reaction.why: I only enquire through a private channel or a referral. Nothing on the page shows they've done my scale, or that discretion is part of how they work. A link next to 'the Get Wedded magazine' feels like a general mailing list, not a private introduction.

top_3_changes: Exclusive use: go beyond 'is it offered'. Old: 'Ask, too, whether another wedding can be held there the same day.' New: 'Ask, too, whether another wedding can be held there the same day, whether the property can stay closed to the public for the whole celebration, and how the venue's own security works alongside a private team.'

Guest numbers: speak to large guest lists and privacy. Old: 'Ask which items are charged per guest, whether there is a minimum spend for your date, and when the final number is locked.' New: 'Ask which items are charged per guest, whether there is a minimum spend for your date, and when the final number is locked. For a very large guest list, ask what size of event the venue has hosted before, and how staff and suppliers are briefed on photos, phones and social media.'

Transfers: acknowledge private travel. Old: '- Who books and pays for transfers on the day, and for arrivals and departures?' New: '- Who books and pays for transfers on the day, and for arrivals and departures, and can private transfers be arranged for family and VIP guests?'

open_questions.question: This post targets Australian couples researching cost; should UHNW low scores be weighted down given it is not a UHNW-intent keyword, or should the post carry a short scale/discretion signal for this segment?
Does Wedded Wonderland have a private or referral enquiry route and verifiable large-scale delivery that the page could reference? I have not assumed either.
